item.title: Wings of Hope awarded $50,000
item.description: CUSHING – Wings of Hope in Cushing has been awarded a $50,000 grant from the Oklahoma Attorney General’s Office to help fully launch its certified Human Trafficking Service Provider program. The funding is part of a $1 million statewide investment announced Feb.

item.title: Sex offender charged with residence violation
item.description: STILLWATER — A 38-year-old man on probation for lewd acts with a child has been jailed on $10,000 bond pending a court appearance this week on a charge accusing him of a residence violation by living across from Cushing High School.

item.title: Cushing leadership approves demolition of vacant buildings
item.description: CUSHING — During a special joint meeting of the Cushing Hospital Authority, Cushing Industrial Authority, and Cushing Education Facilities Authority, city officials approved bids to demolish two vacant structures near the hospital — clearing space for potential future development.

item.title: Officials review aging water line infrastructure
item.description: CUSHING — City officials have taken early steps towards long-term improvements to the community’s water system after reviewing the results of a recent water model and preliminary master plan. Representatives of Professional Engineering Consultant (PEC) gave a detailed presentation on the city’s water infrastructure recently — outlining the current conditions and identifying potential areas for upgrades over the next several years.

item.title: Cushing Airport returns to full FAA compliance
item.description: CUSHING — The City of Cushing has reached an important milestone as its municipal airport has officially been restored to full compliance with the Federal Aviation Administration (FAA), according to city officials.

item.title: Payne County commissioner gives project update
item.description: PAYNE COUNTY — Payne County District 1 Commissioner Zach Cavett shared an update on county infrastructure, funding, and upcoming road projects impacting the area. Cavett highlighted road and bridge improvements funded through the state’s County Improvements for Roads and Bridges (CIRB) program, as well as partnerships with the Sac and Fox and Pawnee Nations to rebuild multiple bridges.

item.title: Benches installed thanks to donation
item.description: CUSHING — Members of the Daughters of the American Revolution (DAR) Cushing Chapter had several commemorative iron benches installed at Cushing Memorial Park and new school complex in honor of America’s upcoming 250th anniversary.

item.title: Cimarron Tower now on National Register of Historic Places
item.description: CUSHING — Cimarron Tower Apartments, formerly known as Hotel Cushing, has been added to the National Register of Historic Places, state officials announced. The Oklahoma Historical Society and the Oklahoma State Historic Preservation Office confirmed March 11 that the downtown Cushing building had received the designation.

item.title: New agreements at airport
item.description: CUSHING — A series of airport related lease agreements were approved by the members of the City of Cushing commission board during their regular monthly meeting on March 16. Commissioners approved multiple rental agreements as well as a ground lease agreement at the Cushing Municipal Airport this past Tuesday.

item.title: City approves ICE bed increase
item.description: CUSHING — The City of Cushing approved a key amendment to its agreement with CoreCivic during Monday’s Board of Commissioners meeting, expanding the number of beds allocated for federal detainees at the Cimarron Correctional Facility.
